sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Raichur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.338/2016, vide judgment and award dated 10.05.2018.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The claimant No.1 is the wife and claimant Nos.2 and 3 were the parents of deceased Bassappa @
Basavaraj, who died in a road accident on 17.12.2012, when he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36/X-7495 which was dashed against by a bus belonging to Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (henceforth referred as 'Corporation') bearing registration No.KA-42/F-912.

The claimants claimed that the deceased NC: 2023:KHC-K:1349 was a driver who had a licence to drive heavy transport vehicle and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month apart from daily allowance of Rs.200/-.

The claimants claimed that due to untimely death of Bassappa,
they were deprived of financial and emotional support and therefore, filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.28,85,000/- from the Corporation.
3. The Corporation contested the claim petition and claimed that the accident was not due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus, but claimed that the deceased was negligent.
It denied the age and occupation of the deceased.
It claimed that it had paid a sum of Rs.50,000/- as compensation.
It claimed since the deceased and the driver of the bus had contributed to the accident, the Corporation was liable to pay only to the extent of 50% of the compensation.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and she marked Exs.P1 to P7.
The NC: 2023:KHC-K:1349 insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and did not mark any documentary evidence.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus.
It also held that the deceased died due to injuries suffered in the accident.
It considered the income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month Smt. Huligemma W/O Late Bassappa vs Sri. V.K.Chowhan S/O Kamal Chawan And ...

on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137655858/
2

and deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:
For loss of dependency Rs.8,32,104/-
For loss of consortium Rs.25,000/-
For loss of love and affection Rs.25,000/-
For loss of estate Rs.25,000/-
For transportation of dead Rs.25,000/-
body and funeral expenses Total Rs.9,32,104/-
6.

The Tribunal directed the Corporation to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of NC:
2023:KHC-K:1349 realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the claimants are in appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the deceased was a driver who possessed licence to drive a heavy transport vehicle and therefore, he was capable of earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month and hence, the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.

She contended that the Tribunal did not consider the loss of future prospects as the deceased was 47 years old and following the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD.
VS. PRANAY SETHI reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25% must have been factored as loss of future prospects.
She contended that the compensation awarded towards loss of consortium and loss of love and affection deserve to be enhanced.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation submitted that the claimants did NC: 2023:KHC-K:1349 not produce the driving licence of the deceased to establish that he was a driver capable of earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.
He therefore contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant interference.
9. I have heard the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation.
10. The accident in question is not in dispute.
The death of Bassappa, aged 47 years is also not in dispute.

The records of the Tribunal disclose that the photocopy of the licence of Sri Bassappa was produced which indicated that as on the date of the accident, Bassappa possessed a licence to drive a heavy Smt. Huligemma W/O Late Bassappa vs Sri. V.K.Chowhan S/O Kamal Chawan And ... on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137655858/
3 transport vehicle.
However, there is no proof of his income.
In that view of the matter, the notional income of Rs.8,000/- per month considered by the Tribunal is just and proper.
However, the Tribunal while determining the compensation must have factored loss of future prospects at 25%.

Similarly, claimant No.1 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1349 being the wife of deceased was entitled to loss of spousal consortium and claimant No.3 was entitled to loss of filial consortium in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

sentences.text: Consequently, the enhanced compensation to which the claimants are entitled to is re-

determined as follows:
Loss of Dependency Rs.10,40,052/-
[Rs.8,000(25%)=10,000(1/3rd)
=Rs.6,667x12x13]
Loss of spousal consortium to Rs.44,000/-

claimant No.1 Loss of filial consortium to Rs.44,000/-
claimant No.3 Loss of estate, transportation Rs.33,000/-
and funeral expenses Total Rs.11,61,052/-
11.

In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.9,32,104/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.11,61,052/-.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.2,28,948/- shall be paid by the Corporation to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the Corporation before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
